items.name: Conditioning
items.category: Unique Techniques (pioneered by The Yoga Institute)
items.introduction: Conditioning is the art of preparing oneself for the right experiences in the present, defined as 'the withdrawal of oneself from the outer as well as from the inner world to attain an emotional calm'. Tendencies, habits and attitudes are the biggest hurdle to progress. Yoga says we have Klishta and Aklishta tendencies; by consciously strengthening Aklishta tendencies we de-condition and recondition ourselves. Conditioning brings faith (self-belief, confidence to begin) and understanding of the purpose and rule of a task. A calm state is not easily acquired in a short time, so the mind is conditioned before any practice. It readies the mind for Asanas, Pranayamas and Kriyas, and can also be practised independently to calm and steady the mind.
startingPosition: Sit in Sukhasana or any other meditative posture and close the eyes. If not possible to sit on the floor, sit on a firm chair with an erect backrest.
Keep the body above the waist straight and the spine erect.
steps: Close the eyes and passively observe the breath for about 10 minutes.
The mind may wander to other thoughts; gently bring it back to the breath.
items.recommendedPractice: Practise daily in the morning and during the day, as required. Maintain the mental state for as long as possible. Remember: 'A quiet mind receives best.'
limitations: No limitations. Can be practised by all.
benefits: Greatly aids in bringing a distracted mind to attentiveness.
Reduces extraneous thoughts.
Brings clarity of thought.

items.name: Anitya Bhavana & Reflection
items.category: Unique Techniques (pioneered by The Yoga Institute)
items.introduction: The human personality cannot be devoid of emotions until it achieves complete control over the mind. Hence Parikarmas, Pratipaksha Bhavana and Anitya Bhavana are recommended to purify the Chitta. Anitya Bhavana is pondering over the transitoriness (Anityata) of all things: the body, objects of pleasure, wealth, youth and opportunities are all changing, so why be attached to anything? Reflection is practised initially to train the mind to become an observer of its own thinking, and is a simplified form of the deeper and more advanced practice of self-study called Anitya Bhavana, a Jain yogic technique. Its objective is to discriminate between what is permanent and what is not.
startingPosition: Sit in Sukhasana/Vajrasana or any other meditative posture and close the eyes. If not possible to sit on the floor, sit on a firm chair with an erect backrest.
steps: Mentally, passively review the events of the previous day in detail and in chronological order.
Do not judge or analyse any thought or event.
Going deeper than mere chronological listing, analyse your state of mind, feelings and even thoughts while living that particular moment.
limitations: No limitations. Can be practised by all.
benefits: End result is the quality of 'mindfulness': awareness of oneself and of the surroundings, and giving one's best in everything one does.
A powerful memory training technique.
We grow only when we learn to observe without the interference of emotions and perceptions.

items.name: Nispandabhava
items.category: Unique Techniques (pioneered by The Yoga Institute)
items.introduction: Nispand means absence of movement. An untrained mind creates problems; a still body leads to a still mind, hence the mind needs to be trained. The technique was developed by Shri Yogendraji, Founder of The Yoga Institute, and helps take the mind out of the body. It develops a 'bystander' or 'witness-like' attitude towards life: detachment and objectivity, leading to an integrated personality that can face life's challenges. Detachment does not mean inaction or complete withdrawal; it is maintaining balance in the midst of chaos and performing duties with ease.
startingPosition: Lean against a wall, resting the head and shoulders, with the legs stretched in front.
Keep a distance of 2-3 feet between the legs, as per individual comfort.
Place the hands gently on the upper thighs with palms facing upwards and close the eyes. If not possible to sit on the floor, sit on a firm chair.
Emphasis is on comfort rather than posture, to minimise distractions.
steps: Start by observing the breath for a few minutes, then gently direct the attention to a sound which is continuous but feeble. If no such sound can be detected, imagine a subtle sound, e.g., the tick-tock of a clock or the strain of a musical instrument.
Passively hear this sound, without any association with the object.
Sit in this posture for 15 minutes. If the mind wanders, gently bring it back to the sound.
items.recommendedPractice: Practise daily in the morning or during the day, as convenient. Remember: 'The subtleties of life can be best understood when the gross ceases.'
limitations: No limitations. Can be practised by all.
benefits: Awareness of the body is gone, which helps the body heal itself without interference by the mind; the body is seen objectively and issues with regard to the body get corrected.
Greatly aids in bringing a distracted mind to attentiveness.
Reduces extraneous thoughts and brings clarity in thinking.

items.name: Yogendra Yonimudra
items.category: Unique Techniques (pioneered by The Yoga Institute)
items.introduction: A technique that facilitates training in Pratyahara or abstraction, withholding the conscious mind from soliciting sensory perceptions. The word Yoni signifies the Ultimate Brahman or Brahmayoni. This unique psycho-physical technique draws inspiration from the tortoise, which withdraws its limbs into its shell the moment it perceives danger, to conserve energy. The senses similarly keep receiving unnecessary and uncontrolled impulses, dissipating mental energy.
startingPosition: Sit in Padmasana or any other meditative posture. If not possible to sit on the floor, sit on a firm chair with an erect backrest.
Keep the body above the waist straight and the spine erect. Eyes closed.
steps: Place the thumbs on the ears and the index fingers resting gently on the eyelids/eyelashes.
Place the middle fingers on the respective nostrils.
The ring fingers are placed above the lips and the little fingers below them. Ensure the elbows are at shoulder level, parallel to the ground.
Passively observe the breath. If the mind wanders, gently bring it back to the breath.
items.recommendedPractice: Practise daily in the morning or during the day, as required. Maintain the mental state for as long as possible. Remember: 'To know the real self, we need to look within and not in the mirror.'
benefits: Helps the mind withdraw the senses and reduces unnecessary chatter.
Provides the required pause needed for a change of perception.
Greatly aids in bringing a distracted mind to attentiveness.
Brings clarity of thought.

items.name: Sahajbhava Asanas
items.sanskritMeaning: For flexibility; Sahaj = to facilitate, bhava = readiness
items.introduction: Due to poor lifestyle and neglect, one suffers pain and stiffness in the body (especially the joints) which reduces flexibility. Regular practice of Sahajbhava Asanas rectifies this. They create awareness of the body and the breath and keep the mind attentive. 'Sahaj' here means to facilitate: the techniques facilitate the body and mind to be established in Sahajbhava, readiness.
preparation: Practise these postures slowly and with full awareness.
Although said to be done standing, most can be done sitting: sit in any meditative posture on a mat or on a straight-back chair without arms.
startingPosition: Stand with the feet slightly apart or at a one-foot distance. Keep the eyes open.
Hold the head straight and the hands by the sides or on the thighs.
Keep the abdomen tucked in and shoulders squared so that an erect posture is maintained.

variations.name: E. Head and Neck - Variation 1 (lateral)
steps: Inhaling, drop the head towards the left shoulder without lifting the shoulder.
Exhaling, bring it back to the centre.
Repeat on the other side.

variations.name: E. Head and Neck - Variation 2 (back and down)
steps: Inhaling, tilt the head backwards as far as possible without moving the shoulders or body, gazing up and back.
Exhaling, bring the head down, tucking the chin into the throat cavity.
Inhaling, return to the centre.

variations.name: E. Head and Neck - Variation 3 (turn)
steps: Inhaling, turn the head to look far right.
Exhaling, return to the centre.
Repeat on the other side.

variations.name: E. Head and Neck - Variation 4 (rotation)
steps: Inhaling, drop the head to the right and gently rotate it, taking it back, from right to left to reach the left shoulder.
Exhaling, return to the straight starting position. There is no forward bending of the head; do it in one gentle continuous motion.
Repeat starting from the left (clockwise and anti-clockwise rotation).

variations.name: F. Shoulders - Variation 1
steps: Hands by the sides. Inhaling, lift the shoulders as high as possible towards the ears to form a 'cup'.
Exhaling, relax the shoulders.

variations.name: F. Shoulders - Variation 2
steps: Rotate the shoulders from back, down while exhaling and then front, upwards while inhaling. Can be done with each shoulder separately too.

variations.name: F. Shoulders - Variation 3
steps: Place the fingers on the respective shoulders, elbows touching each other in front.
Rotate the shoulders, raising the elbows up in front and then outwards while inhaling, and down to come back in front to the starting position while exhaling.
Now rotate in the opposite direction: exhaling, move the elbows downwards and outwards, then inhaling, up to return to the starting position.

variations.name: F. Shoulders - Variation 4
steps: Keep the arms relaxed and straight by the side.
Rotate them by the side, clockwise and then anti-clockwise. Can be done with each arm separately too.

variations.name: G. Hands - Variation 1
steps: Clasp the hands in front of the chest, fingers intertwined and palms facing the chest.
Inhaling, stretch them outwards, parallel to the floor.
Exhaling, bring them close to the chest.

variations.name: G. Hands - Variation 2
steps: Same as Variation 1, except that while stretching the hands the palms are turned out, away from the chest.

variations.name: G. Hands - Variation 3
steps: Clasp the hands above the head, fingers intertwined and palms facing down.
Inhaling, stretch them upwards, straightening the elbows.
Exhaling, bring them down towards the head, bending the elbows.

variations.name: G. Hands - Variation 4
steps: Same as Variation 3, except that while stretching, the palms are turned out towards the ceiling.

variations.name: G. Hands - Variation 5
steps: Keeping the hands straight, clasp them at the back with fingers intertwined.
Inhaling, raise the arms upwards as far as possible, keeping the trunk straight.
Exhaling, relax and bring the hands down.

variations.name: G. Hands - Variation 6
steps: Take both hands behind and join the palms (fingers pointing up) to form Namaskara Mudra at the back. Hold for 5 seconds; breathe normally.

variations.name: G. Hands - Variation 7
steps: Take the right hand up; fold it to let the palm fall behind the neck, elbow pointing upwards.
Take the left hand behind and fold it to clasp the fingers of the right hand.
Practise both sides alternately; breathe normally.

variations.name: G. Hands - Variation 8
steps: Interlace the fingers at the back of the neck, elbows pointing out in front.
Inhaling, move the elbows towards their respective sides; exhaling, bring them back to the front.

variations.name: H. Elbows
steps: Raise both arms in front, at shoulder level. Inhale.
Exhaling, bend the elbows and touch the shoulders with the fingers.
Inhaling, straighten the arms again. Repeat a few times.

variations.name: I. Wrists - Variation 1
steps: Raise the arms in front at shoulder level.
Close the fingers and rotate the fists clockwise and then anti-clockwise.

variations.name: I. Wrists - Variation 2
steps: Raise the arms to the sides at shoulder level, palms facing down.
Keeping the arms straight, flap the palms up and down.

variations.name: J. Trunk - Variation 1 (side bend)
steps: Stand with the feet 20-24 inches apart, hands on the waist.
Gazing straight ahead, bend the trunk to the right, inhaling. Keep hips and legs fixed; only curve the spine.
Exhaling, return to the centre. Repeat to the left.

variations.name: J. Trunk - Variation 2 (back and forward bend)
steps: Gazing straight ahead, bend backwards, arching the spine, inhaling. Hips and legs fixed.
Exhaling, return to the centre and bend forward.
Inhaling, return to the centre.

variations.name: J. Trunk - Variation 3 (twist)
steps: Gazing straight ahead, exhaling, turn right, twisting the spine.
Inhaling, return to the centre. Repeat to the left.

variations.name: K. Knees - Variation 1
steps: Stand erect, gazing straight ahead.
Tighten the knees and then relax them, alternately.

variations.name: K. Knees - Variation 2
steps: Balance on the left leg and bend the right knee, exhaling.
Inhaling, bring it down to the floor. Repeat bending the left knee.

variations.name: K. Knees - Variation 3
steps: Balance on the left leg and lift the right leg from the hip.
Bend the right knee to keep the thigh parallel to the floor.
Holding the thigh up, rotate the right knee clockwise and anti-clockwise. Repeat with the left leg.

variations.name: K. Knees - Variation 4
steps: Stand erect with the feet together.
Bend forward and cup the knees with the respective palms.
Rotate the knees, keeping the feet fixed, clockwise and anti-clockwise.

variations.name: L. Ankles - Variation 1
steps: Balance on the left leg, lift the right leg from the hip and bend the knee to keep the thigh parallel to the floor.
Holding the thigh up, point the toes outwards and then inwards several times. Repeat for the left leg.

variations.name: L. Ankles - Variation 2
steps: Take the first 2 steps of Variation 1.
Holding the thigh up, rotate the foot clockwise and anti-clockwise. Repeat for the left leg.

items.recommendedPractice: Practise slowly with full awareness, coordinating movement with breath (as given in each variation).
limitations: No limitations for people with reasonably good health; those with specific problems can practise sitting or lying down.
Can be practised by all, as per individual comfort.
Exceptions: post-surgery, or as specified by a physician.
benefits: Results in a leaner and stronger body.
Functions as 'warm-up' stretches, imperative to any asana session; loosens taut muscles.
Helps initiate the flow of blood and energy through the body.
Provides a gentle but deep internal awakening of the musculature into action.
Breathing rhythms aid energy flow to each cell.
Builds immunity against several infectious ailments.
Keeps one fit and youthful.

items.name: Surya Namaskar
items.introduction: The sun symbolises spiritual consciousness and has been worshipped daily since ancient times. Surya Namaskar is relatively a modern practice and is not regarded as a traditional part of Hatha Yoga. It is a warm-up routine based on a sequence of seven asanas, of which five are repeated twice, making a twelve-step salutation.
startingPosition: Stand erect with the hands at the sides and the feet as close together as possible.
Hold the neck straight, abdomen in normal contour (deflated at its lower end but not necessarily drawn in), and chin drawn in.
Focus the eyes at one point straight ahead, keeping the mind calm and body relaxed.
steps: Fold both hands in Namaskar Mudra in front of the chest; shoulders and elbows relaxed; passively observe the breath (Sthitaprarthanasana).
Exhale, release the mudra and take the hands down. Inhaling, raise the straight arms above the head, bending the trunk slightly backwards (Hasta-uttanasana). No movement below the waist.
Exhaling, bend forward from the waist, legs straight, head between the hands; hands down beside the feet and forehead close to the knees (Hastapadasana).

Inhaling, bend the left knee between the hands (palms on the floor) and take the right leg behind as far as possible, right knee off the floor; raise the head and arch the spine backwards (Ashwa Sanchalanasana).

Exhaling, move the left foot behind next to the right, about 1 foot apart; straighten the arms and raise the hips to bring the head (facing down) between the arms; knees and elbows straight, heels resting on the floor (Adho Mukha Shvanasana).
Inhaling, lower the body; exhaling, let the toes, knees, chest, hands and chin touch the floor with the hips slightly up; maintain with the breath suspended (Ashtanga Namaskara).
Inhaling, lower the hips and raise the head, palms on the floor (shoulders pulled down, elbows soft); arch the back (Bhujangasana).
Exhaling, lower the trunk and raise the hips to bring the head between the arms; knees and elbows straight, heels on the floor (Adho Mukha Shvanasana, as in step 5).
Inhaling, bend the right knee forward between the hands and take the left leg behind as far as possible; raise the head and arch the spine (Ashwa Sanchalanasana).
Exhaling, bring the left leg next to the right, palms flat beside the feet, straighten both knees and bring the forehead close to the knees (Hastapadasana).
Inhaling, raise both arms and head, straighten the back and then arch gently backwards (Hasta-uttanasana, as in step 2).
Exhaling, straighten the trunk, bring the hands down, then hold the palms in Namaskar Mudra in front of the chest, feet together (Sthitaprarthanasana, as in step 1).
Repeat the same sequence taking the left leg behind in Ashwa Sanchalanasana (step 4) and the left leg forward in step 9. This completes one round.
After mastering the poses, there is an option to practise with the mantras of Surya Namaskar.
items.recommendedPractice: Practise 1-2 rounds, as per individual comfort, with a pause between rounds.
limitations: Refer to the limitations/contraindications of the respective asanas.
benefits: Physical: influences the health of the entire body; stimulates and improves all organs; strengthens neck, shoulders, arms, wrists, fingers, back, stomach, waist, abdomen, intestines, thighs, knees, calves and ankles; invigorates the nervous system; reduces redundant fat (abdomen, hips, thighs, neck, chin).

Therapeutic: alleviates digestive ailments and constipation; helps elimination of toxins; improves vital capacity of the lungs, endocrine functioning and the quality and circulation of blood; improves knock knees in walking; helps cope with insomnia; helps regulate the menstrual cycle.
Psychological: gives poise, mental as well as physical; increases concentration, optimism and self-confidence; increases emotional strength and spiritual growth.
